# Historical layers and optional stack

Show change over time through a source layout, not a copied company history. Keep historical Classic ASP, VBScript, VB6/COM and T-SQL material inert. Use original annotations to distinguish what learners can inspect from what runs.

A separate local path may illustrate WebForms on open-source Mono/XSP, a .NET API, PostgreSQL and a reverse proxy. Make it clear which component owns a seat hold, which claims need checking, and which dependencies are optional. A simple rule or random number in a demonstration is not a trained model.

The default frontend must work without this stack. Keep assets local, preserve applicable third-party notices, and never depend on a legacy executable, network service or database to start quest 01.
